title: Infinity Yoneda and pointwise mapping-space limit calculus
statement:
Use the infinity categories and universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and the mapping-space and coherent-diagram conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Write $\mathcal S$ for the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small spaces. It admits all $\mathcal U$-small limits. For every infinity category $\mathcal E$ fitting in $\mathcal U'$ and having $\mathcal U$-small mapping spaces, the infinity categories $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E,\mathcal S)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ admit $\mathcal U$-small limits, computed objectwise (the functor categories themselves may be large relative to $\mathcal U$). More generally, for a small simplicial set $K$ and an infinity category $\mathcal V$, every small limit or colimit diagram in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V)$ is characterized objectwise whenever the corresponding limits or colimits exist in $\mathcal V$. In particular, when $\mathcal V$ has all small colimits, colimits in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal V)$ exist and their source and target are the corresponding colimits in $\mathcal V$. The Yoneda functor $j:\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, $j(e)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(-,e)$, is fully faithful.

For every small coherent diagram $p:J\to\mathcal E$, a cone with apex $l$ is limiting if and only if its induced maps $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,l)\to\lim_{j\in J}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,p(j))$ are equivalences, naturally in $x$. Dually a cocone with apex $c$ is colimiting if and only if $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(c,x)\to\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(p(j),x)$ is an equivalence for every $x$. In particular, covariant representable mapping-space functors preserve all existing small limits, and contravariant representables take all existing small colimits to limits. These equivalences are natural in the diagrams and in the testing objects.

proof.text:
Let $F:J\to\mathcal S$ with $J$ small. By [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] choose its left-fibration representative $E_F\to J$ with small total simplicial set, and put $M=\operatorname{Fun}_{/J}(J,E_F)$. This is a small Kan complex: it is the mapping complex over $J$ from the identity left fibration to $E_F$, and in each degree it is a subset of the set of maps between two small simplicial sets. For a small Kan complex $X$, the same classification, its constant-functor clause and the exponential identity of simplicial sets give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal S)}(\Delta_JX,F)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/J}(J\times X,E_F)=\operatorname{Fun}(X,M)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(X,M).$$
The last comparison is the classification over a point, which identifies its mapping complex with maps between Kan complexes. These comparisons are natural in $X$. Write $\Phi_X$ for the displayed equivalence from transformations to maps into $M$, and choose $\lambda:\Delta_JM\to F$ with $\Phi_M(\lambda)\simeq1_M$. For $a:X\to M$, naturality and composition compatibility give $\Phi_X(\lambda\circ\Delta_Ja)\simeq\Phi_M(\lambda)\circ a\simeq a$, on the entire mapping space. Since $\Phi_X$ is an equivalence, composition with $\lambda$ is its inverse and is therefore an equivalence. The limiting-cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes this a limit. For $J=\varnothing$ the section complex is a point, so the construction includes the terminal object.

source.place: Limits-of-spaces construction, section-space model; comparison with arbitrary constant Kan-complex diagrams

proof.text:
Fix small $J$, a simplicial parameter $K$ in a sufficiently large universe, and a diagram $P:J\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V)$. Currying, given degreewise by rearranging the factors $J\times K\times\Delta^n$, gives $\widetilde P:K\to\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal V)$. Let $\mathcal D_0$ be the full subcategory of $J$-diagrams admitting a limit, and assume every $\widetilde P(k)$ belongs to it; fullness makes $\widetilde P$ factor through $\mathcal D_0$. Apply [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] with $T=\Delta_J:\mathcal V\to\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal V)$. A limiting cone is precisely a universal arrow $\Delta_J l\to Q$, by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so the hypothesis holds on $\mathcal D_0$. Its parameter clause supplies $L=R\widetilde P:K\to\mathcal V$ and a cone $\lambda:\Delta_J L\to P$ such that, for every $A:K\to\mathcal V$,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V)}(A,L)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V))}(\Delta_JA,P).$$
Hence $\lambda$ is a limit by the same cone criterion, and each evaluated cone is its universal-arrow component, hence is limiting.

proof.text: For any other cone $\mu:\Delta_JH\to P$, the universal equivalence of Step 2 supplies $u:H\to L$ with $\lambda\Delta_Ju\simeq\mu$. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], if $\mu$ is limiting then both cones are terminal in the same cone quasicategory, whose full terminal-object subcategory is Kan; hence this cone comparison, and its apex $u$, are equivalences. Conversely, if $u$ is invertible, the cone test for $\mu$ is the cone test for $\lambda$ precomposed with $\operatorname{Map}(A,u)$ for each $A$; using the inverse of $u$ makes that map an equivalence, so $\mu$ is limiting. The same argument at each vertex $k$, with the evaluated limit $\lambda(k)$ of Step 2, gives $\mu(k)$ limiting if and only if $u(k)$ is invertible. The vertexwise-equivalence clause of the cited node now proves the objectwise recognition assertion. Only the evaluated diagrams were assumed to have limits; no completeness of $\mathcal V$ or smallness of $K$ in the smaller universe was used.

source.place: Agent argument through partial universal arrows; pointwise limit assertion dual to the stated colimit assertion

proof.text: Apply Steps 2-3 to $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $K^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversing simplicial orders identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal V^{\mathrm{op}})$ and reverses cones into cocones. Thus the same existence and recognition assertions hold for colimits. With $K=\Delta^1$, evaluation at its two vertices gives exactly the source and target colimit statements. Finally take $\mathcal V=\mathcal S$, $K=\mathcal E$ or $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$, and use Step 1: both space-valued functor categories have small limits, regardless of their larger size. Only the diagram shape $J$ and values of $F$ in Step 1 were required to be small.

source.place: Opposite and universe specializations of Steps 2-3

proof.text:
For $p:J\to\mathcal E$ and $x\in\mathcal E$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-constant-source-section-comparison] to get
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)}(\Delta_Jx,p)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal S)}(\Delta_J*,H_{\mathcal E}(x,p(-))).$$
Step 1 with $F=H_{\mathcal E}(x,p(-))$ and $X=*$ identifies the right side with its small limit: $\Phi_*$ identifies it with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(*,M)\simeq M$. The comparison node explicitly allows the original arrow-family total space to be only $\mathcal U'$-small; its section space has a small model. For a specified cone $\lambda:\Delta_Jl\to p$, the comparison identifies postcomposition on $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,l)$ with $f\mapsto(\lambda_j\circ f)$, including higher coherence. Thus the universal-arrow test for $\lambda$ in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] is exactly the assertion that
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,l)\longrightarrow\lim_{j\in J}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,p(j))$$
is an equivalence for every $x$. This proves both implications of the mapping-space limit criterion with the actual cone-induced comparison.

source.place: Section models and the mapping-space tests for cones; the argument uses arbitrary fixed-source arrow families

proof.text:
A cocone $p\to\Delta_Jc$ is a cone in $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ on $p^{\mathrm{op}}:J^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply Step 5 there. The identities $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,c)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(c,x)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,p(j))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(p(j),x)$ are not equalities: the right-pinched space of $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the left-pinched space of $\mathcal E$. Reversing simplices identifies $U_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)$ with $U_{\mathcal E}(y,x)$ degreewise, since $(\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Delta^1$ swaps the endpoints; [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] in $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ and in $\mathcal E$ gives the two equivalences with right-pinched spaces, naturally in the endpoints. On the diagram level, the source-fixed arrow left fibration of $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ at $x$ is the opposite of the target-fixed arrow right fibration of $\mathcal E$ at $x$, so by [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] $H_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,p(-))$ and $H_{\mathcal E}(p(-),x)$ classify the same fibration over $J^{\mathrm{op}}$. These comparisons identify its criterion with the required equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(c,x)\longrightarrow\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(p(j),x).$$
The cocone legs give the comparison by precomposition, exactly the opposite of the postcomposition comparison of Step 5. Applying the forward directions of these two criteria to any existing limit cone or colimit cocone gives the claimed preservation by covariant and contravariant representable functors.

proof.text:
Curry the coherent bifunctor of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] to obtain $j(e)=H_{\mathcal E}(-,e)$ and choose the equivalent right-fibration model $\mathcal E_{/e}\to\mathcal E$ supplied there and in [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. For any $F:\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$ represented by $q:E_F\to\mathcal E$, classification gives
$$\operatorname{Map}(j(e),F)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/\mathcal E}(\mathcal E_{/e},E_F).$$
The identity vertex $1_e$ is final in $\mathcal E_{/e}$: apply [lem-coef-infinity-slice-equivalence-final] to the equivalence edge $1_e$. Thus $\{1_e\}\hookrightarrow\mathcal E_{/e}$ is right anodyne by [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-anodyne]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] to $q$ and this inclusion, and pull its displayed map back over the fixed base map $\mathcal E_{/e}\to\mathcal E$. This yields the restriction map
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{/\mathcal E}(\mathcal E_{/e},E_F)\longrightarrow(E_F)_e\simeq F(e)$$
as a trivial Kan fibration. Its lifting property survives the pullback by solving the same lifting square upstairs and retaining its prescribed base map. By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] it is a homotopy equivalence. All these arguments may be made in $\mathcal U'$; they do not require $\mathcal E$ to be $\mathcal U$-small. Now take $F=j(e')$. The composite is evaluation at $1_e$, so its composite with the map induced by $j$ on $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(e,e')$ is $u\mapsto u\circ1_e$, naturally homotopic to the identity on that entire mapping space. Since evaluation is an equivalence, the map induced by $j$ is an equivalence. This proves full faithfulness, with the actual Yoneda map identified rather than an unspecified equivalence between the two spaces.

proof.text: The equivalences in Step 1 are the transport comparison followed by the simplicial exponential identity; Step 2 uses the specified universal-arrow transformation and its evaluation compatibility; Step 5 restricts the same arrow family and takes its section complex. Thus precomposing in the testing object, or changing the coherent diagram, commutes with these comparisons up to the coherences already supplied by transport and universal arrows. The canonical comparison of each cone with the chosen limit is defined by its own universal property, not by a choice of independent objectwise identifications. The opposite constructions retain the same compatibilities. This proves the stated naturality in diagrams and testing objects. Explicitly, for $a:x'\to x$, a family $(b_j:x\to p(j))$ restricts to $(b_j\circ a)$; for a coherent transformation $t:p\to p'$, it maps to $(t_j\circ b_j)$. The comparison of a specified cone $\lambda$ sends $f:x\to l$ to $(\lambda_j\circ f)$. These formulas commute by the composition and unit coherences in the transport node. For higher simplices use the representing simplicial mapping complexes in the transport classification: composition of simplicial maps and restriction along $\Delta^m\to\Delta^n$ commute. The coherent classification comparison carries these identities to the arrow families displayed in Step 5 and gives the corresponding coherent compatibility on spaces. No strictly chosen composition operation in $\mathcal E$ is needed.
